title: Elastic Response Quanta — sketch notes
content:
Topline idea: provide an abstraction that lets the platform expose discrete 'response quanta' (buckets of response fidelity/compute) that can be chosen per-request, per-session, or by policy. The goal: give product teams predictable token dollars + fidelity tradeoffs without having to manage many model variants or bespoke prompt engineering for each customer.

Motivation / problem we're solving:
- Teams need simple knobs for cost vs quality on live user traffic. Right now they pick models (gpt-x/opt-xx) or fiddle with temperature/stop tokens which is messy.
- Many apps have multiple interaction types (quick suggestion vs multi-turn summary) but the platform treats them uniformly.
- Customers want SLA+cost predictability for high-volume flows.

Core concept (very rough):
- Define a set of named quanta (e.g., nano, micro, standard, premium). Each quantum maps to a small bundle of runtime decisions: target p50 latency, token budget, model family preference, quantization mode, KV-cache policy, and optional post-processing steps (abbreviation, compression).
- Runtime uses the quantum to pick model variant and execution config. If primary route unavailable, fall back to a cheaper quantum (graceful degrade).
- Quanta can be attached to routes, API keys, or session templates. A single API request may provide an override header.

MVP scope (what we can ship fast):
- UX: simple UI in Console where teams define 3 quanta: micro (low cost), balanced, fidelity (high quality). Basic sliders: token cap, target latency, cost multiplier hint.
- API: accept a `response_quanta` field for generation endpoints (string). Default maps to 'balanced'.
- Serving: routing logic in controller layer that maps quantum -> model variant + batching profile. Implement fallback to cheaper quantum when capacity constrained.
- Metrics: per-quantum token counts, p90/p50 latency, quality proxy (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or cheap semantic similarity to reference prompts for test set).

User stories:
- As a growth PM I want a low-cost quantum for lightweight autocomplete flows so I can keep usage cheap while scaling.
- As a platform engineer I want an automatic fallback so customer apps stay up during high load, with predictable drop in fidelity.
- As a product designer I want to limit worst-case latency for premium users even if cost is higher.

Operational considerations:
- How to pick model family automatically? heuristic: if sequence length < 256 and quantum == micro -> tiny quantized model, else standard model family. Maintain a catalog mapping.
- Autoscaling: micro quantum should be eligible for higher batching to reduce cost; fidelity quantum should have latency-first routing.
- Telemetry: label all traces with quantum to enable billing and quality analysis. Need to add taxonomy in console + DB dimension.

Quality measurement plan:
- Create small QA prompt suite across three canonical flows (short answer, summarization, instruction). For each quantum, capture semantic-similarity to golden outputs and token cost. Track regression alerts if similarity drops > X while cost increases > Y.

APIs and SDK changes:
- generation endpoint: add optional header `X-Response-Quanta: micro|balanced|fidelity` and body field `response_quanta` for SDKs.
- Console: route-level default and per-api-key override. Allow templates: e.g., chatbot-default = balanced, search-snippets = micro.

Possible rollout strategy:
- Alpha: internal dev teams + 2 pilot customers. Default mapping: micro -> gpt-mini-q4, balanced -> gpt-std-q8, fidelity -> gpt-std-q4-large.
- Beta: gate to customers via feature flag + opt-in in console.
- GA: expose to all with recommended policies and cost-savings calculator in Console.

Open design questions / risks:
- How granular should quanta be? Too many -> decision complexity; too few -> not useful. Start small (3).
- Does mapping become a maintenance burden as model catalog changes? Need automated compatibility checks and an onboarding vetting job that validates mappings each release.
- Billing / metering: do we mark tokens with quantum tag and bill differently? Probably yes; need alignment with billing team.
- User expectations: falling back to cheaper quantum may degrade semantics; need dark launching and clear documentation.

Experiment ideas (cheap experiments to validate concept):
- A/B test: route 10% of traffic to micro for a single search task, measure retention and task success vs balanced.
- Simulation: replay historical traffic against different quantum mappings to estimate token savings and latency distribution.

Implementation appendix (engineer notes, rough tasks):
- Controller: add quantum dimension to routing table + fallback policy implementation (2d matrix: quantum x capacity-state -> chosen-quantum).
- Runtime: expose batching and latency hints via model serving config. Add flag to prefer lower-precision kernels for micro quantum.
- Console: UI for creating quanta, mapping to routes and templates. Persist definitions in existing config-service.
- Telemetry: add tag `response_quanta` to traces, metrics, and usage events. Billable event includes quanta id.

Next actions (short):
- Sync with billing and console PMs (Priya) — align on tagging and UI constraints.
- Create JIRA spike to prototype routing matrix + simulate with 2 days of replay data.
- Build a 1-week internal hack: enable micro quantum for internal search to get empirical numbers.

Random notes / heuristics (handy):
- micro = best-effort shorter latencies, aggressive prefix cache reuse, token cap 64–128.
- balanced = default, token cap 512, standard kernels.
- fidelity = p95 latency soft limit, larger token cap, higher-precision kernels, smaller batch sizes.

Questions to resolve in the sync:
- SLA implications: do quanta have explicit SLAs? probably only fidelity has higher SLOs.
- Multi-tenant isolation concerns if quanta map to cheaper spot capacity.
- How to represent quanta in audit logs for compliance?

End — raw brain dump. Will tidy into a short PRD if we decide to pursue.
